gaps.sentence: Show me ___ you have written so far.
gaps.explanation: 'What you have written' means 'the things that you have written'; 'that' cannot head a nominal clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: This is the worst storm ___ we have had for years.
gaps.hint: after a superlative ('the worst'), use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'That' follows superlatives in defining relative clauses; 'which' is considered poor style there.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.

gaps.sentence: His latest film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject pronoun for the film; 'that' never appears in non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The candidate ___ speech impressed us most got the job.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose speech' — the speech belonged to the candidate.

gaps.sentence: We have reached the point ___ we must decide whether to continue.
gaps.explanation: 'The point where ...' is a standard abstract use of 'where', meaning 'at which'.
